chosen_property.label: recordedOutcome
chosen_property.definition: Officially documented or noted a specific outcome.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property directly connects Country to Event as a documentation relation; minting new property 'recordedOutcome'.

candidates.label: recordedIn
candidates.comment: A recording capture relation between an event and the creative work that captured all or part of it. Also called captured by, documented in, featured in. Examples: "A concert event was recorded in 'a live album'.", "A historical event was recorded in 'a documentary film'.", "A speech event was recorded in 'a news broadcast'.". Distinct from recordedAt, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: recordedAt
candidates.comment: A recording location relation between a creative work and the event where it was recorded. Also called recorded during, captured at event. Examples: "A live album was recorded at 'Wembley Stadium Concert'.", "A documentary film was recorded at 'the Amazon Rainforest Expedition'.", "A podcast episode was recorded at 'a conference panel discussion'.". Distinct from recordedIn, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: recordedAs
candidates.comment: A recording relation between a music composition and an audio recording of that work. Also called recorded version, audio rendition. Examples: "A music composition 'Symphony No. 5' is recorded as 'Berlin Philharmonic recording'.", "A song 'Yesterday' is recorded as 'The Beatles' original recording'.", "A classical piece is recorded as 'a live performance album'.". Distinct from recordingOf, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: resultComment
candidates.comment: The specific comment created or sent as the outcome of a comment or reply action. Also called generated comment, comment outcome, produced comment. Examples: `CommentAction on Article` resultComment `User's Comment Text`, `ReplyAction to Forum Post` resultComment `Reply Comment`, `ReviewAction` resultComment `Reviewer's Feedback`. Distinct from `result`, which is a general outcome of any action.

candidates.label: resultReview
candidates.comment: The specific review created as the outcome of a review action. Also called generated review, review outcome, produced review. Examples: `ReviewAction on Product` resultReview `Customer's Product Review`, `ReviewAction on Movie` resultReview `Critic's Movie Review`, `ReviewAction on Service` resultReview `User Service Feedback`. Distinct from `result`, which is a general outcome of any action.

candidates.label: result
candidates.comment: The outcome or product generated by an action. Also called outcome, product, output, consequence. Examples: `WriteAction` result `Book`, `CookAction` result `Meal`, `CreateAction` result `Artwork`. Distinct from `resultComment` and `resultReview` which are specific types of results.

candidates.label: recordingOf
candidates.comment: A recording of relation between a music recording and the music composition it represents. Also called rendition of, version of, based on composition. Examples: "A music recording 'Bohemian Rhapsody' is a recording of 'the Queen composition'.", "A classical track is a recording of 'Beethoven's Symphony No. 9'.", "A cover song is a recording of 'the original composition'.". Distinct from recordedAs, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: observationDate
candidates.comment: The date or date and time when an observation was made. Also called date of observation, observation timestamp, recorded date. Examples: "Weather Observation observationDate '2023-10-27'", "Medical Observation observationDate '2023-10-26T14:30:00'", "Astronomical Observation observationDate '2023-09-15'". Distinct from observationPeriod, which is the duration of the observation.

candidates.label: knownVehicleDamages
candidates.comment: A vehicle condition relation between a vehicle and a textual description of its known damages, whether repaired or not. Also called vehicle damage report, damage history, known defects, condition notes. Examples: A used car has knownVehicleDamages 'minor dent on rear bumper'. A vehicle has knownVehicleDamages 'repaired fender bender'. A truck has knownVehicleDamages 'scratches on passenger side door'. Distinct from vehicleCondition, which is a general assessment, not specific damages.

candidates.label: claimReviewed
candidates.comment: A summary relation for a claim review, providing a short text of the specific claims being reviewed. Also called "reviewed claim", "claim summary", "subject of review". Examples: "Fact-check review claimReviewed 'Eating apples cures cancer'", "Product claim review claimReviewed 'This product doubles battery life'".

chosen_property.label: subjectOf
chosen_property.justification: Reused 'subjectOf' in inverse direction (Event is about Country).

candidates.label: experienceInPlaceOfEducation
candidates.comment: An experience in place of education relation indicating whether a job posting accepts relevant experience as an alternative to formal educational qualifications. Also called: experience substitutes education, education equivalency, alternative qualification. Examples: "Senior Developer Job" experience in place of education "true", "Entry-Level Marketing Position" experience in place of education "false", "Project Manager Role" experience in place of education "true".

candidates.label: experienceRequirements
candidates.comment: An experience requirements relation between a job posting or occupation and the necessary skills and experience for the role. Also called: required experience, skill requirements, professional background. Examples: "Software Engineer Job" experience requirements "5+ years in Java development", "Marketing Manager Occupation" experience requirements "Proven track record in digital marketing campaigns", "Chef Position" experience requirements "Culinary school degree and 3 years restaurant experience".

candidates.label: monthsOfExperience
candidates.comment: A required number of months of experience for an occupational role. Also called experience duration, minimum experience, required experience in months. Examples: "Software Engineer Role monthsOfExperience 24", "Marketing Manager Position monthsOfExperience 60", "Entry-level Job monthsOfExperience 0".

candidates.label: skills
candidates.comment: The competencies, knowledge, or abilities possessed by a person or organization, or required for a job or occupation. Also called competencies, abilities, qualifications, expertise. Examples: `Job Posting: Software Engineer` skills `"Python, Java, SQL"`, `Person: Jane Doe` skills `"Project Management, Public Speaking"`, `Occupation: Doctor` skills `"Diagnosis, Patient Care"`. Distinct from `qualifications`, which are formal requirements.

candidates.label: proficiencyLevel
candidates.comment: A proficiency level relation between a technical article and the skill level required to understand its content. Also called skill level, required expertise, target audience level. Examples: "A Python tutorial has a proficiency level of 'Beginner'.", "A deep learning research paper has a proficiency level of 'Expert'.", "A guide to advanced calculus has a proficiency level of 'Intermediate'."

candidates.label: sensoryRequirement
candidates.comment: A description, defined term, or URL detailing the sensory abilities (e.g., hearing, vision) required for a job. Also called sensory abilities, perceptual requirements, job sensory needs. Examples: `Call Center Job` sensoryRequirement `"Excellent hearing"`, `Graphic Designer Role` sensoryRequirement `"Normal color vision"`, `Pilot Position` sensoryRequirement `URL to FAA medical standards`. Distinct from `physicalRequirement`, which is about physical capabilities.

candidates.label: seriousAdverseOutcome
candidates.comment: A severe complication or side effect, such as death, disability, or life-threatening conditions, that may result from a medical device or therapy. Also called severe side effect, major complication, critical adverse event. Examples: `Chemotherapy` seriousAdverseOutcome `Severe Immunosuppression`, `Surgical Procedure` seriousAdverseOutcome `Infection`, `Medical Device Implant` seriousAdverseOutcome `Device Malfunction Leading to Injury`. Distinct from `adverseOutcome`, which is a more general adverse event.

candidates.label: knowsAbout
candidates.comment: A knowledge domain relation between an organization or person and a topic or entity they possess knowledge about. Also called knowledgeable about, familiar with topic, understands, has expertise in (without implying skill level). Examples: A person knowsAbout 'artificial intelligence'. An organization knowsAbout 'renewable energy policy'. A researcher knowsAbout 'quantum physics'. Distinct from hasOccupation or alumniOf, which are about formal roles or education, not general knowledge.

candidates.label: timeRequired
candidates.comment: A duration representing the approximate time typically needed for an audience to engage with or complete a creative work. Also called "completion time", "estimated duration", "reading time", "viewing time". Examples: "The article has timeRequired 10 minutes", "The course's timeRequired is 40 hours", "This creative work takes timeRequired 2 hours to watch."

candidates.label: attendee
candidates.comment: A person or organization present at an event. Also called: participant, guest, visitor. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendee 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendee 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendee 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendees, which is the plural form.

relations.definition: A person or organization explicitly stated a position or assertion.
relations.embedding_query_text: made claim about: A person or organization explicitly stated a position or assertion.

chosen_property.label: subjectOf
chosen_property.justification: Reused 'subjectOf' in inverse direction (GovernmentStatement is about GovernmentOfficial).

candidates.label: claimInterpreter
candidates.comment: An interpretation relation between a claim and the organization or person who interpreted it from media content. Also called "interpreted by", "claim analyst", "fact-checker". Examples: "News claim claimInterpreter FactCheck.org", "Social media claim claimInterpreter Jane Doe".

candidates.label: interpretedAsClaim
candidates.comment: A claim extraction relation between a creative work or media object and a specific assertion or statement derived from its content. Also called contains claim, implies claim, claim extracted from, claim derived from. Examples: A news article is interpretedAsClaim 'The sky is blue'. A scientific paper is interpretedAsClaim 'Drug X cures Y'. A video is interpretedAsClaim 'Candidate Z made promise A'.

candidates.label: legalRepresentative
candidates.comment: A legal representation relation between an organization and the person(s) authorized to act on its behalf in legal matters. Also called authorized representative, legal agent, official representative, corporate officer. Examples: An organization has a legalRepresentative of 'its CEO'. A company's legalRepresentative is 'its sole administrator'. The board appointed 'Jane Doe' as legalRepresentative. Distinct from employee, which is a general employment relation, not specifically legal representation.

candidates.label: namedPosition
candidates.comment: A specific named position or role played by a person or organization within a larger organization. Also called role name, position title, job title. Examples: "Athlete Role namedPosition 'Quarterback'", "Employee Role namedPosition 'Senior Software Engineer'", "Board Member Role namedPosition 'Treasurer'". Distinct from roleName, which is a more general description of a role.

candidates.label: spokenByCharacter
candidates.comment: An attribution relation between a quotation and the character, person, or organization to whom it is attributed within a creative work. Also called "attributed to", "quote speaker", "character says", "uttered by". Examples: "The quote is spokenByCharacter Hamlet", "The dialogue was spokenByCharacter the CEO", "This line is spokenByCharacter a fictional narrator."

candidates.label: creator
candidates.comment: An authorship relation between a creative work or user comment and the person or organization responsible for its creation. Also called: author, originator, producer, made by. Examples: "Novel" creator "Jane Doe", "Software" creator "Acme Corp.", "Blog Post" creator "John Smith", "User Review" creator "Anonymous User". Distinct from copyrightHolder, which is about legal ownership.

candidates.label: owner
candidates.comment: A person or organization that owns a thing. Also called proprietor, possessor, title holder. Examples: "Car owner 'John Doe'", "Company owner 'Acme Corp'", "House owner 'Smith Family Trust'". Distinct from creator, who made the thing.

candidates.label: legislationCountersignedBy
candidates.comment: A countersignature relation between a piece of legislation and the person or organization that countersigned it. Also called: countersigned by, officially endorsed by, co-signed by. Examples: "The Bill of Rights legislationCountersignedBy President Washington", "EU Directive 2023/45 legislationCountersignedBy European Commission", "Local Ordinance legislationCountersignedBy City Clerk".

candidates.label: unnamedSourcesPolicy
candidates.comment: An unnamed sources policy relation between a news media organization or organization and a statement about its policy on using unnamed sources. Also called anonymous sources policy, source confidentiality policy, disclosure policy. Examples: "NewsMediaOrganization unnamedSourcesPolicy 'https://example.com/sources-policy'", "Organization unnamedSourcesPolicy 'Our policy requires two independent sources.'", "News outlet unnamedSourcesPolicy 'https://example.com/ethics'".

candidates.label: founder
candidates.comment: A founder relation between an organization and the person or organization that established it. Also called: established by, created by, initiated by. Examples: "Microsoft" founder "Bill Gates", "Apple Inc." founder "Steve Jobs", "Google" founder "Larry Page". Distinct from founders, which is specifically for multiple people.

chosen_property.label: subjectOf
chosen_property.justification: Reused 'subjectOf' as-is (Continent is subject of Event).

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: studySubject
candidates.comment: An investigative relation between a medical study and the medical entity (condition, therapy, drug, etc.) that is being investigated. Also called "subject of investigation", "research focus", "entity studied", "trial subject". Examples: "The medical study has studySubject a new drug", "The clinical trial's studySubject is a specific medical condition", "This study investigates a studySubject therapy."

candidates.label: guidelineSubject
candidates.comment: A guideline subject relation between a medical guideline and the medical conditions, treatments, or other entities it addresses. Also called: guideline topic, subject matter, focus. Examples: "AHA Guideline for Hypertension" guideline subject "Hypertension", "NICE Guideline for Diabetes" guideline subject "Type 2 Diabetes", "WHO COVID-19 Guidelines" guideline subject "COVID-19". Distinct from guideline, which is the guideline itself.

candidates.label: itemReviewed
candidates.comment: A review subject relation between an aggregate rating or review and the entity that is being evaluated or rated. Also called reviewed item, rated item, subject of review, evaluated entity. Examples: A review has an itemReviewed of 'Restaurant X'. An aggregate rating has an itemReviewed of 'Movie Y'. A product review has an itemReviewed of 'Smartphone Z'. Distinct from itemOffered, which is the subject of an offer or demand.

candidates.label: itemOffered
candidates.comment: A transaction subject relation between a demand or offer and the specific item, product, service, or event being requested or provided. Also called offered item, demanded item, subject of offer, product/service offered. Examples: An offer has an itemOffered of 'a new car'. A demand has an itemOffered of 'web design service'. An offer has an itemOffered of 'a concert ticket'. Distinct from itemReviewed, which is the subject of a review, not an offer/demand.

candidates.label: mainEntity
candidates.comment: A main entity relation between a creative work and the primary entity it describes. Also called: primary subject, about entity, central topic. Examples: "Wikipedia Article mainEntity Albert Einstein", "News Report mainEntity The Election", "Research Paper mainEntity Quantum Physics". Distinct from mainEntityOfPage, which indicates the page for which this thing is the main entity.

candidates.label: followee
candidates.comment: A followee relation between a follow action and the person or organization that is being followed. Also called: followed entity, subject of follow, target of follow. Examples: "User A follows User B" followee "User B", "Fan follows Band X" followee "Band X", "Journalist follows News Organization Y" followee "News Organization Y". Distinct from follows, which is the general social relation.

candidates.label: spatialCoverage
candidates.comment: A geographic focus relation between a creative work and the place(s) that are the primary subject or focus of its content. Also called "geographic scope", "covered area", "location focus", "content location". Examples: "A weather dataset has spatialCoverage New York State", "The historical map's spatialCoverage is ancient Rome", "This research paper's spatialCoverage is the Arctic region.". Distinct from spatial, which is a more general spatial association when the specific focus is not known.

candidates.label: aspect
candidates.comment: A specific area or topic of medical practice considered on a medical webpage. Also called: medical topic, health aspect, clinical focus. Examples: "MedicalWebPage 'Diabetes' aspect 'diagnosis'", "MedicalWebPage 'Flu' aspect 'treatment'", "MedicalWebPage 'Cancer' aspect 'prognosis'."

chosen_property.label: contentReferenceTime
chosen_property.justification: Reused 'contentReferenceTime' as-is (Schedule describes time of Event).

candidates.label: timestamp
candidates.comment: A timestamp relation between an instantaneous event and the specific date and time it occurred. Also called event time, occurrence time, moment of event. Examples: "Concert timestamp 2023-10-27T20:00:00", "Login timestamp 2023-11-01T09:30:15Z", "Photo timestamp 2023-05-15T14:22:00".

candidates.label: contentReferenceTime
candidates.comment: A temporal reference relation for a creative work, indicating the specific date and time described or emphasized within its content. Also called "event time", "depicted time", "time of content". Examples: "News article contentReferenceTime '2023-10-26T14:00:00Z'", "Historical documentary contentReferenceTime '1945-09-02'".

candidates.label: scheduledTime
candidates.comment: The specific date or date and time when an action is planned to occur. Also called planned time, scheduled date, appointment time. Examples: `Meeting Action` scheduledTime `2023-10-26T10:00:00`, `Delivery Action` scheduledTime `2023-11-01`, `Maintenance Action` scheduledTime `2023-12-05T14:30:00`.

candidates.label: doorTime
candidates.comment: A door time relation between an event and the date or time when admission will commence. Also called "admission time", "entry time", "gate opening time". Examples: "Concert event doorTime '19:00'", "Theater show doorTime '2023-11-01T18:30'", "Festival doorTime '10:00'".

candidates.label: endDate
candidates.comment: An end date relation between an item (such as a season, event, or schedule) and the date and time when it concludes. Also called "conclusion date", "finish date", "termination date". Examples: "Event 'Conference' endDate '2023-10-27'", "Creative work season endDate '2024-05-31'", "Role 'Project Manager' endDate '2025-12-31'". Distinct from endTime, which specifies the end time within a single day or for a clip.

candidates.label: departureTime
candidates.comment: A temporal event relation between a trip and its expected departure time. Also called: scheduled departure, leaving time, takeoff time. Examples: "Flight" departure time "2023-11-01T08:00:00Z", "Bus Trip" departure time "14:30:00", "Train Journey" departure time "2023-12-25T10:00:00". Distinct from arrivalTime, which is the expected arrival time.

candidates.label: duration
candidates.comment: A duration relation between an item (such as an event, media object, or schedule) and its length of time. Also called "length", "time span", "period". Examples: "Movie 'Avatar' duration 'PT2H42M'", "Event 'Concert' duration 'PT3H'", "Audio recording duration 'PT5M30S'". Distinct from durationOfWarranty, which is specifically about warranty length.

candidates.label: repeatFrequency
candidates.comment: A repeat frequency relation between a schedule and the interval at which events will recur. Also called recurrence interval, event frequency. Examples: "A meeting schedule has a repeat frequency 'weekly'.", "A workout plan has a repeat frequency 'every other day'.", "A subscription service has a repeat frequency 'monthly'."

candidates.label: previousStartDate
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the previously scheduled start date for an event that has been rescheduled or cancelled. Also called original start date, former start date, initial event date. Examples: A rescheduled event has a previous start date of '2023-03-15'. The cancelled concert had a previous start date of '2023-07-01T19:00:00'. The postponed meeting's previous start date was 'last Monday'. Distinct from startDate, which is the current or newly scheduled start date.

candidates.label: coverageEndTime
candidates.comment: A temporal boundary relation between a live blog posting and the time when its event coverage concludes. Also called: coverage end, reporting end time, live blog conclusion. Examples: "Election Night Live Blog" coverage end time "2024-11-06T04:00:00Z", "Sports Event Live Update" coverage end time "2023-07-15T19:30:00Z", "Conference Live Blog" coverage end time "2023-10-27T17:00:00Z". Distinct from coverageStartTime, which indicates when coverage begins.

chosen_property.label: reached
chosen_property.definition: A temperature value reached in a country.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property fits QuantitativeValue to Country in this context; minting 'reached'.

candidates.label: contactPoint
candidates.comment: A communication relation between a health insurance plan, organization, or person and one of their contact points. Also called "contact info", "point of contact", "reach at". Examples: "Company organization contactPoint 'Customer Service'", "Person contactPoint 'Email Address'". Distinct from contactPoints, which is the plural form, though semantically similar.

candidates.label: contactPoints
candidates.comment: A communication relation between an organization or person and their various contact points. Also called "contact information", "points of contact", "ways to reach". Examples: "Company organization contactPoints [Customer Service, Press Office]", "Person contactPoints [Email, Phone]". Distinct from contactPoint, which is the singular form, though semantically similar.

candidates.label: arrivalBusStop
candidates.comment: An arrival bus stop relation between a bus trip and the station or stop where it concludes. Also called destination bus stop, final bus station. Examples: "A bus trip's arrival bus stop is 'Grand Central Station'.", "The bus trip's arrival bus stop is 'Main Street Stop'."

candidates.label: arrivalBoatTerminal
candidates.comment: An arrival boat terminal relation between a boat trip and the terminal or port where it concludes. Also called destination boat terminal, disembarkation port. Examples: "A boat trip's arrival boat terminal is 'Port of Miami'.", "The ferry trip's arrival boat terminal is 'Dover Terminal'."

candidates.label: expectedArrivalFrom
candidates.comment: An expected arrival from relation between a parcel delivery and the earliest date or datetime the package is anticipated to arrive. Also called: earliest arrival, minimum delivery date, estimated start arrival. Examples: "Amazon Order #123" expected arrival from "2023-10-26", "UPS Package #456" expected arrival from "2023-10-27T09:00:00", "International Shipment" expected arrival from "2023-11-01". Distinct from expectedArrivalUntil, which is the latest arrival date.

candidates.label: arrivalTerminal
candidates.comment: A terminal identifier for a flight's arrival location. Also called: flight destination terminal, terminal of arrival. Examples: "Flight BA286 arrivalTerminal 'Terminal 5'", "Flight from Tokyo arrivalTerminal 'North Terminal'", "Flight to JFK arrivalTerminal 'Terminal 4'". Distinct from arrivalStation, which is for train trips.

candidates.label: expectedArrivalUntil
candidates.comment: An expected arrival until relation between a parcel delivery and the latest date or datetime the package is anticipated to arrive. Also called: latest arrival, maximum delivery date, estimated end arrival. Examples: "Amazon Order #123" expected arrival until "2023-10-28", "UPS Package #456" expected arrival until "2023-10-27T17:00:00", "International Shipment" expected arrival until "2023-11-05". Distinct from expectedArrivalFrom, which is the earliest arrival date.

candidates.label: distance
candidates.comment: A distance relation between an exercise action or travel action and the length travelled. Also called "travelled distance", "route length", "journey distance". Examples: "Exercise action 'Running' distance '10 km'", "Travel action 'Road Trip' distance '500 miles'", "Cycling activity distance '25 mi'".

candidates.label: greater
candidates.comment: A greater relation indicating that one qualitative value is superior or larger than another. Also called: is greater than, exceeds, is more than. Examples: "High" greater "Medium", "Excellent" greater "Good", "Large" greater "Small". Distinct from greaterOrEqual, which includes equality.

candidates.label: availableFrom
candidates.comment: A date and time when an item is available for pickup from a store or locker. Also called: pickup start time, ready for collection. Examples: "DeliveryEvent 'Package' availableFrom '2023-10-27T10:00:00'", "DeliveryEvent 'Order' availableFrom '2023-10-28'". Distinct from availableThrough, which specifies the end of pickup availability.

relations.definition: A component of a larger system or phenomenon.
relations.embedding_query_text: is part of: A component of a larger system or phenomenon.

instances: France -> Europe

chosen_property.label: isPartOf
chosen_property.justification: Reused 'isPartOf' as-is (Country is part of Continent).

candidates.label: isPartOf
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation indicating that an item or creative work is a component of a larger creative work or resource. Also called component of, member of, contained in, element of. Examples: A chapter isPartOf 'a book'. An episode isPartOf 'a TV series'. A web page isPartOf 'a website'. Distinct from hasPart, which expresses the inverse relationship (the whole *has* a part).

candidates.label: subEvent
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a larger event and a smaller event that is a component or part of it. Also called "part of event", "component event", "nested event", "event within event". Examples: "The conference has subEvent a keynote speech", "The festival's subEvent is a specific concert", "This event includes a subEvent workshop.". Distinct from superEvent, which points from the smaller event to the larger one.

candidates.label: partOfSystem
candidates.comment: A biological relation between an anatomical structure and the anatomical or organ system it is a component of. Also called is a component of, belongs to, is found in, forms part of. Examples: The heart is part of the circulatory system. The lungs are part of the respiratory system. A bone is part of the skeletal system.

candidates.label: subEvents
candidates.comment: A collection of hierarchical relations between a larger event and multiple smaller events that are components or parts of it. Also called "component events", "nested events", "events within event", "parts of event". Examples: "The conference has subEvents multiple presentations", "The festival's subEvents include several concerts and workshops", "This event comprises many subEvents.". Distinct from subEvent, which refers to a single component event.

candidates.label: isPartOfBioChemEntity
candidates.comment: A biochemical part-whole relation indicating that one biochemical entity is a component of another larger biochemical entity. Also called component of biochem entity, contained within biochem entity, element of biochem entity. Examples: A protein domain isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a larger protein'. A subunit isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a protein complex'. A specific gene sequence isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a chromosome'.

candidates.label: superEvent
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a smaller event and the larger event of which it is a part. Also called "part of larger event", "parent event", "contained within event", "main event". Examples: "The concert has superEvent the music festival", "The presentation's superEvent is the conference", "This workshop is part of a superEvent summit.". Distinct from subEvent, which points from the larger event to the smaller one.

candidates.label: subStructure
candidates.comment: A component relation between an anatomical structure and the smaller anatomical structures that comprise it. Also called "component structure", "anatomical part", "composed of", "contains structure". Examples: "The heart has subStructure atria", "The brain's subStructure includes the cerebrum", "This anatomical structure is made up of several subStructure elements."

candidates.label: subTrip
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a larger trip and a smaller trip that is a component or segment of it. Also called "trip segment", "part of trip", "daily itinerary", "trip leg". Examples: "The multi-day journey has subTrip Day 1", "The grand tour's subTrip is the visit to Rome", "This trip includes several subTrip components."

candidates.label: hasPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a creative work and another creative work that is a component of it. Also called includes part, contains component, component of. Examples: "A book has a part that is a chapter.", "A symphony has a part that is a movement.", "A website has a part that is a specific page.". Distinct from includedComposition, which is specific to music compositions.

candidates.label: parentService
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a broadcast service and a broader broadcast service it is a variation or component of. Also called belongs to, is a variation of, is part of, is a channel of. Examples: BBC One Scotland is a parent service of BBC One. A regional news channel is a parent service of a national news channel. A specific sports channel is a parent service of a broader sports network.

relations.definition: A subsequent event or condition that succeeds another.
relations.embedding_query_text: followed by: A subsequent event or condition that succeeds another.

chosen_property.label: followedBy
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property directly links HeatwaveForecastEvent to Event in this context; minting 'followedBy'.

candidates.label: nextItem
candidates.comment: A list item that immediately follows the current list item in an ordered sequence. Also called subsequent item, following item, next in list. Examples: "Item 1 nextItem 'Item 2'", "Page 3 nextItem 'Page 4'", "Step A nextItem 'Step B'". Distinct from previousItem, which links to the preceding item.

candidates.label: previousItem
candidates.comment: A sequential relation between a list item and the list item that immediately precedes it. Also called precedes, comes after, follows. Examples: List item 'B' has a previous item 'A'. The current item's previous item is the one before it. In a breadcrumb trail, the current page has a previous item. Distinct from nextItem, which links to the item that follows.

candidates.label: follows
candidates.comment: A follows relation representing a generic uni-directional social connection between two people. Also called: is following, subscribes to, tracks. Examples: "Alice follows Bob", "Charlie follows David", "Eve follows Frank". Distinct from followee, which is the object of a follow action.

candidates.label: eventStatus
candidates.comment: An event status relation between an event and its current status type. Also called "event condition", "status of event", "event state". Examples: "Event 'Concert' eventStatus 'EventCancelled'", "Event 'Meeting' eventStatus 'EventScheduled'", "Event 'Festival' eventStatus 'EventRescheduled'".

candidates.label: tocContinuation
candidates.comment: A table of contents continuation relation between a HyperToc entry and the next default HyperToc entry to play or render. Also called next entry, subsequent entry, continued by. Examples: "Chapter 1 tocContinuation 'Chapter 2'", "Segment A tocContinuation 'Segment B'", "HyperTocEntry 'Intro' tocContinuation 'Main Content'".

candidates.label: followee
candidates.comment: A followee relation between a follow action and the person or organization that is being followed. Also called: followed entity, subject of follow, target of follow. Examples: "User A follows User B" followee "User B", "Fan follows Band X" followee "Band X", "Journalist follows News Organization Y" followee "News Organization Y". Distinct from follows, which is the general social relation.

candidates.label: predecessorOf
candidates.comment: A lineage relation between a product model and its newer, often superseding, variant. Also called replaced by, succeeded by, updated to, newer version is. Examples: iPhone 10 is a predecessor of iPhone 11. Model A is a predecessor of Model B. The old software version is a predecessor of the new one. Distinct from successorOf, which points from a newer variant to an older one.

candidates.label: supersededBy
candidates.comment: A deprecation relation between an older term (property, class, or enumeration) and a newer term that replaces or supersedes it. Also called "replaced by", "obsoleted by", "succeeded by", "deprecated by". Examples: "OldProperty is supersededBy NewProperty", "The deprecated class is supersededBy a modern equivalent", "This enumeration value is supersededBy a more precise one."

candidates.label: error
candidates.comment: An error relation between a failed action and the thing providing more information on the cause of the failure. Also called "failure cause", "problem details", "issue description". Examples: "Action 'Payment' error 'Insufficient Funds'", "Action 'Login' error 'Invalid Credentials'", "Action 'File Upload' error 'File Too Large'". Distinct from errorCode, which is a specific code for the error.

candidates.label: followup
candidates.comment: A followup relation between a medical procedure and the typical or recommended post-procedure care. Also called: aftercare, post-procedure care, follow-up instructions. Examples: "Surgery" followup "Rest for 2 weeks, avoid heavy lifting", "Dental Cleaning" followup "Brush twice daily, floss regularly", "Vaccination" followup "Monitor for side effects, schedule booster shot".

candidates.label: foodWarning
candidates.comment: A food warning relation between a drug and any precautions, guidance, or contraindications regarding food consumption while taking it. Also called: dietary restrictions, food interactions, consumption advice. Examples: "Warfarin" food warning "Avoid grapefruit, limit Vitamin K rich foods", "Antibiotics" food warning "Do not take with dairy products", "MAOIs" food warning "Avoid aged cheeses and cured meats".

candidates.label: alcoholWarning
candidates.comment: An alcohol warning relation between a drug and any precautions or contraindications regarding alcohol consumption while using it. Also called alcohol interaction, drinking advisory, alcohol caution. Examples: "A medication's alcohol warning states 'Do not consume alcohol'.", "The drug's alcohol warning advises 'Limit alcohol intake'."

candidates.label: pregnancyWarning
candidates.comment: A medical attribute providing precautions, guidance, or contraindications regarding a drug's use during pregnancy. Also called pregnancy precautions, drug-pregnancy risks, maternal warnings. Examples: A drug has a pregnancy warning 'Consult doctor before use'. The medication includes a pregnancy warning about 'potential fetal harm'. There is a pregnancy warning against 'use in first trimester'.

candidates.label: breastfeedingWarning
candidates.comment: Any precaution, guidance, or contraindication related to a drug's use by breastfeeding mothers. Also called: lactation warning, nursing caution, breastfeeding safety. Examples: "Drug 'Medication X' breastfeedingWarning 'Consult doctor before use'", "Drug 'Drug Y' breastfeedingWarning 'Not recommended for breastfeeding mothers'."

candidates.label: contraindication
candidates.comment: A medical restriction relation for a medical device or therapy, indicating a contraindication. Also called "medical warning", "precaution", "not recommended for". Examples: "Drug therapy contraindication 'Pregnancy'", "Medical device contraindication 'Pacemaker users'".

candidates.label: safetyConsideration
candidates.comment: Any potential safety concerns, interactions, or adverse reactions associated with a dietary supplement. Also called supplement warnings, safety warnings, adverse effects. Examples: `St. John's Wort` safetyConsideration `"May interact with antidepressants"`, `Creatine Supplement` safetyConsideration `"Not recommended for individuals with kidney issues"`, `Vitamin D Supplement` safetyConsideration `"Avoid excessive dosage"`.

candidates.label: expertConsiderations
candidates.comment: An expert considerations relation between a diet and the medical expert advice pertinent to that dietary plan. Also called: medical advice, professional guidance, health warnings. Examples: "Keto Diet" expert considerations "Consult a doctor if you have kidney issues", "Vegan Diet" expert considerations "Ensure adequate B12 supplementation", "Low-Sodium Diet" expert considerations "Monitor blood pressure regularly".

candidates.label: risks
candidates.comment: The specific physiological dangers or adverse effects associated with a particular diet plan. Also called diet hazards, health risks of diet, diet side effects. Examples: `Keto Diet` risks `"Nutrient deficiencies"`, `Fad Diet` risks `"Metabolic imbalance"`, `Vegan Diet` risks `"Vitamin B12 deficiency if not supplemented"`.

candidates.label: accessibilityHazard
candidates.comment: An accessibility hazard relation between a creative work and a characteristic that poses a physiological danger to some users. Also called accessibility risk, dangerous feature, user hazard. Examples: "A video's accessibility hazard is 'flashingLights'.", "A game's accessibility hazard is 'motionSimulation'."

candidates.label: isRelatedTo
candidates.comment: A general association relation between two products or services that have some unspecified connection. Also called associated with, connected to, linked to, relevant to. Examples: A smartphone isRelatedTo 'a smart watch'. A car service isRelatedTo 'car insurance'. A book isRelatedTo 'a movie adaptation'. Distinct from isSimilarTo, which implies functional similarity, and isAccessoryOrSparePartFor or isConsumableFor, which imply specific functional dependencies. This is a very general relation.

candidates.label: relatedStructure
candidates.comment: A related structure relation between an anatomical system and structures that connect to or are associated with it, but are not part of the system itself. Also called associated structure, connected structure. Examples: "The circulatory system has a related structure 'the heart'.", "The nervous system has a related structure 'the brain'.", "The digestive system has a related structure 'the liver'."

candidates.label: relatedAnatomy
candidates.comment: A related anatomy relation between superficial anatomy and other anatomical structures or systems connected to it. Also called associated anatomy, connected to anatomy. Examples: "The skin of the forearm has related anatomy 'radius bone'.", "The superficial muscles of the back have related anatomy 'vertebral column'.", "The scalp has related anatomy 'cranium'."

candidates.label: temporal
candidates.comment: A general temporal relation between a creative work and a date or time, used when more specific temporal properties are not applicable. Also called "related to time", "time context", "associated temporal period", "timeframe". Examples: "The novel has temporal the 19th century", "The painting's temporal is the Renaissance era", "This document's temporal is the year 2020.". Distinct from temporalCoverage, which indicates the specific time period the content applies to.

candidates.label: relatedTo
candidates.comment: A familial relation between two people, representing a generic family connection. Also called family member, kin, relative. Examples: "John is related to 'Jane'.", "Mary is related to 'Tom'.", "Aunt Sally is related to 'Nephew Bob'."

candidates.label: connectedTo
candidates.comment: A connection relation between an anatomical structure and other anatomical structures it is connected to. Also called "linked to", "adjoins", "connects with". Examples: "Femur anatomical structure connectedTo Tibia", "Brain anatomical structure connectedTo Spinal cord".

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: associatedAnatomy
candidates.comment: An anatomical structure, system, or superficial anatomy related to a medical condition or physical activity. Also called: related anatomy, anatomical connection, affected anatomy. Examples: "MedicalCondition 'Arthritis' associatedAnatomy 'Knee Joint'", "PhysicalActivity 'Running' associatedAnatomy 'Leg Muscles'", "MedicalCondition 'Migraine' associatedAnatomy 'Brain'."

candidates.label: subjectOf

Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

Examples: "The quote is spokenByCharacter Hamlet", "The dialogue was spokenByCharacter the CEO", "This line is spokenByCharacter a fictional narrator."

candidates.label: creditedTo

candidates.label: causeOf

Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: cause
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical condition and its medical cause. Also called "etiology", "origin", "caused by". Examples: "Flu medical condition cause Influenza virus", "Heart attack medical condition cause Coronary artery disease". Distinct from causeOf, which describes what a medical cause leads to, whereas cause describes what leads to a condition.

candidates.label: evidenceOrigin

Examples: "AHA Guideline for Hypertension" evidence origin "RCT", "NICE Guideline for Diabetes" evidence origin "Consensus Opinion", "WHO Guideline for COVID-19" evidence origin "Observational Studies". Distinct from evidenceLevel, which is the strength of the evidence.

candidates.label: sourceOrganization

Also called "commissioning organization", "producing organization", "organization behind", "publisher organization". Examples: "The research paper's sourceOrganization was MIT", "The documentary's sourceOrganization was BBC", "This report's sourceOrganization is the World Health Organization."

candidates.label: sourcedFrom

Also called "originates from", "nerve pathway source", "derived from brain structure". Examples: "The optic nerve is sourcedFrom the diencephalon", "Cranial nerve V is sourcedFrom the brainstem", "This nerve's neurons are sourcedFrom the spinal cord."

candidates.label: citation
candidates.comment: A reference relation between a creative work and another creative work or text that it cites. Also called "reference", "cited work", "source". Examples: "Research paper citation 'Smith, J. (2020). Article Title.'", "Blog post citation 'https://example.com/article'".

candidates.label: contributor

Also called "additional contributor", "supporting role", "collaborator". Examples: "Book creative work contributor 'Editor Jane Doe'", "Conference event contributor 'Sponsor Acme Corp'". Distinct from author or creator, which typically denote primary responsibility.
